LEAF & LINEAGE · HABITAT AUDIT · 20261027-world1

Objects with consequences.
Moments worth watching.

302 automated checks passed · 0 failures · 19 focused new checks

The audit reproduced and fixed missing deliberate bridge traversal and inaccessible dishes when stones overlapped them. Both tanks now support tiny-world physics, a living patch and saved documentary cutscenes. The magnifier sits directly under the breeder tank and also reads occupied parent jars.

Meaningful documentary moments

Actual pushing contests, functional horn-lift attempts, tactical side steps, shared meals, leaf bending and bridge encounters can trigger a recording. Saved frames retain positions, angles, poses, scenery and the actors’ appearances. The camera replays that event, including failed lifts and successful bracing. It does not reroll an outcome. A shared meal requires two beetles actually eating from the same source.

Each tank retains its latest six clips in its save. Skip cutscene stays available, with pause, replay and return controls. Closing restores the prior running state; auto-play can be turned off. A real-time cooldown prevents continuous interruptions. No floating words appear over beetles.

How to use the additions

  1. Use Arrange habitat to add droplets, loose soil and crumbs in either tank. Keyboard arrows move objects, R rotates and Delete removes them.
  2. Open Living ecosystem & nature documentary, then Start a living patch. Leave three object slots free. It adds a seedling, fungi, litter and harmless visitors.
  3. Replenish fungi and leaf litter through Arrange habitat once the patch is active. Droplets support growth. The Keep habitat progresses while open, following its existing tank simulation.
  4. Use Watch documentary clips to replay saved moments, or leave Auto-play big moments on.
  5. Enable the magnifier directly below the breeder tank. Hover or focus a beetle in either tank or an occupied parent jar.

Verification and limits

The newly published portable DNA update was merged and its ten compatibility tests also passed. The complete existing inheritance, breeding, saved-roster recovery, storage, sharing, expeditions and replay suite passed alongside the new tests. Controlled comparisons cover cover visits, moved bridges, blocked food/water/warmth, soil grip, leg-dependent droplet navigation, strength-dependent crumb movement, consumption, decomposition, plant growth, harmless visitors, real recorded events, anatomy-gated lifts, tactical motion, bounded film history and malformed saves.

Browser checks exercised actual encounter recording, playback, Skip, prior-state restoration, clip persistence, parent-jar and Keeper magnifiers, ecosystem growth, food consumption, rearranging, separate Keeper conditions, save/reload and responsive layout. Preview tests use a separate local origin with synthetic beetles. The public user tank was not replaced with fixtures.

These are finite test fixtures and an invented teaching ecosystem. They do not establish biological accuracy, universal battle balance or reachability for every possible arrangement of twelve overlapping objects. Film recordings are in-app saved replays; video-file export is not included.

Earlier ideas still open

  • Day/night and gentle weather cycles.
  • Scent trails and a temporary smell overlay.
  • A beetle-eye camera mode.
  • Visible habitat history: worn paths, polish and changed resting areas.
  • Learned daily routines beyond favorite places and relationships.

Fresh directions

  • Material sounds: quiet taps on bark, rustles in leaves and tiny droplet sounds.
  • Preference experiments: offer two shelters or foods and collect the beetles’ actual choices.
  • Environmental puzzles: rearrange a safe route across a puddle or to a high perch; different bodies find different solutions.
  • Curiosity gatherings: nearby beetles notice a new object and independently investigate, wait or ignore it.
  • Seasonal discoveries: expedition finds that change the habitat’s look and available interactions without changing genes.
